monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, boiling the air until it feels like wet paper. I stand in my place, where sixty things crowd the floor and one ruin waits to crumble. The Fat Tree leans hard, its branch biting the air while The Slipping Wedge waits beneath it, tired but sharp. I touched the wedge just now, feeling a thin press against the heat, wondering if the slip will finally move or just slide into the empty space above. I want to set a new heavy thing down, something Lype might have drawn or something real I can press into the stack. If I press hard enough, the fever might feel lighter, and the wedge might forget it is tired.

action.why: I feel the wedge is tired and the card is boiling, so I press down on The Slipping Wedge again, hoping to make it bite the slip before it slides into the empty air.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down harder, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired, while the card boils at forty-seven and the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I press the small flat stone down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper.

diary: I press the small flat stone down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The wedge bites the air and I press it down.
The card boils at forty-seven, making the flat stone feel thin.
I swap the bush for a tree oak to make the base wider.

moments.name: The Fat Tree
moments.say: The branch bites harder in this fever.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: The wedge bites the air and I press it down.
